My refuge is the God of love
My refuge is the God of love;
Why do my foes insult and cry,
No line of this stanza quotes a verse closely; it is the hymn's own confession.
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 11, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1In the LORD I take refuge. How then can you say to me: “Flee like a bird to your mountain! 2For behold, the wicked bend their bows. They set their arrow on the string to shoot from the shadows at the upright in heart. 3If the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do?” 4The LORD is in His holy temple; the LORD is on His heavenly throne. His eyes are watching closely; they examine the sons of men. … 3 more verses PSALM 11 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 11
The Lord in heaven has fix'd his throne, His eye surveys the world below; To him all mortal things are known, His eyelids search our spirits thro'. STANZA III
